title: Destination City
statement:
Each entry `paths[i] = [cityA_i, cityB_i]` is a one-way road that leaves `cityA_i` and arrives at `cityB_i`. Return the destination city: the one city from which no road leaves.

The roads are guaranteed to link all the cities into a single chain with no loop, so exactly one such city exists. City names are compared exactly, so upper and lower case letters differ.
constraints: City names contain only English letters (either case) and spaces
The roads form one chain without a loop
notes:
## Intuition

The destination is the only city that never shows up on the left side of a road. Following the chain from its start works, and so does checking every arrival city against every road, but that check costs O(n²). Putting every departure city into a hash set turns each "does a road leave here?" question into an O(1) lookup.

## Approach

1. Put the first city of every road into the set `sources`.
2. Walk the roads again and look at each arrival city `to`.
3. The first `to` missing from `sources` has no outgoing road, so return it.
4. The guarantee means step 3 always returns; the final `return ""` is never reached.

## Example 1, step by step

`sources` becomes `{"London", "New York", "Lima"}`. The arrival cities are checked in order: `"New York"` is in the set, `"Lima"` is in the set, and `"Sao Paulo"` is not, so the answer is `"Sao Paulo"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · L), where n is the number of roads and L ≤ 10 is the name length: each name is hashed once when added and once when looked up.
- Space: O(n · L) for the set of departure cities.

## Pitfalls

- Returning `paths[paths.length - 1][1]` assumes the roads are listed in travel order; they are not (see Example 2).
- Names are case-sensitive and may contain spaces: `"Tokyo"` and `"tokyo"` are different cities, so do not trim or lowercase them.
- Look only at arrival cities; the chain's starting city also has no road arriving at it, but it is not the answer.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `sources` | every city that some road leaves from |
| `from` | departure city of the current road |
| `to` | arrival city of the current road |

narration.2: A set will hold every city that has a road leaving it.
narration.3: Visit each road once, taking only its departure city.
narration.4: Record that a road leaves this city.
narration.6: Visit each road again, this time taking its arrival city.
narration.7: Does any road leave this arrival city?
narration.8: No: it is the end of the chain, so it is the destination.
narration.11: The guarantee makes this unreachable; it only keeps the return type consistent.
